topic.angle: Peter I's beard tax and the beard token

body.claim: In 1698, Tsar Peter I of Russia instituted a beard tax. Men who paid it were required to carry a copper or silver "beard token".
body.why: It was part of an effort to bring Russian society in line with Western European models. Resistance was widespread, since many believed a beard was a religious requirement. Financially, the tax was unsuccessful: few people were unwilling to shave, and the state overestimated its ability to administer and collect it.

probes.question: What were men who paid Russia's beard tax required to carry?
True or false: from a financial standpoint, Russia's beard tax was unsuccessful.

image_brief.show: A Russian beard token (copper coin-like token with a face and beard)
